description: A four-panel composite figure of a triplex (ferrite-austenite-martensite) low-density steel annealed at 950 °C/1 h; the panels are of three different kinds. (a) is a colour-coded EBSD Phase Map (PM) with a 50 μm scale bar; legend entries are Ferrite (green), Martensite (yellow) and Austenite (red). A dominant green ferrite matrix carries elongated, broadly aligned yellow martensite and red austenite bands plus isolated blocky austenite. (b) is a TEM bright-field micrograph (1 μm scale bar) of a large γ (labelled 1) region containing a dark banded ά phase inside an α matrix; white arrows mark boundaries the caption calls initial ferrite–ferrite boundaries. Three SAED insets labelled 1, 2, 2 give zone axes Z=[001], Z=[011], Z=[111] with indexed reflections. (c) plots True Stress (MPa, 0–600) versus True Strain (0.0–0.6) for compression at 500 °C (black) and 600 °C (red): the 500 °C curve peaks near the 550–560 MPa level then softens, while 600 °C plateaus around 400 MPa. (d) is an inset of Stress (Mpa) versus Deformation Temperature (°C, 100–700) for Maximum Flow Stress and Yield Stress (0.2%), with a blue dashed oval marking the steep drop between 500 and 600 °C. Together the panels show that this banded triplex structure loses strength sharply above 500 °C.

observations.observation: Panel (a) legend identifies the EBSD phase map colours as Ferrite (green), Martensite (yellow) and Austenite (red), and the scale bar is labelled 50 μm.
Panel (a) shows a green ferrite matrix with elongated yellow martensite and red austenite bands aligned along a common banding direction, plus isolated blocky red austenite regions.

Panel (b) is a TEM bright-field micrograph with a 1 μm scale bar in which α, γ and a dark banded ά region are labelled, with white arrows marking boundaries the caption calls the initial ferrite–ferrite boundaries.
Three SAED patterns in (b), labelled 1, 2 and 2, carry printed zone axes Z=[001], Z=[011] and Z=[111] with indexed reflections including (200), (111), (211), (011), (101) and (110).
Panel (c) contains exactly two curves labelled 500 °C (black) and 600 °C (red) on axes True Stress (MPa) 0–600 versus True Strain 0.0–0.6.

In (c) the 500 °C curve rises to a maximum between the 500 and 600 MPa gridlines (near 550–560 MPa) and then gradually decreases toward true strain 0.6, whereas the 600 °C curve sits close to the 400 MPa level.

Panel (d) plots Stress (Mpa) versus Deformation Temperature (°C) with a legend distinguishing Maximum Flow Stress and Yield Stress (0.2%), and a blue dashed oval highlights the steep drop between 500 and 600 °C.
The caption states the material is a triplex (ferrite-austenite-martensite) low density steel annealed at 950 °C/1 h.
The caption states the compression tests in (c) were performed at a strain rate of 0.001 s⁻¹ at 500 and 600 °C.
The caption states panel (d) shows extracted stress levels versus temperature over the wide range 100–700 °C.
The citing text states that band slope phase contrast was used as a qualitative approach to differentiate martensite from ferrite, both having a BCC crystal structure, as depicted in Fig. 1a.
The citing text states the initial microstructure was compressed to a true strain of 0.6 over a temperature range of 100–700 °C, summarised in Fig. 1c.

The citing text states the flow curve is mechanically stable over 200–500 °C but shows a significant drop in stress level when the temperature increases from 500 to 600 °C, indicated by the blue dashed oval in Fig. 1d.
The citing text attributes appreciable flow softening after a true strain of 0.3 in the 500–600 °C curves to strain induced transformation rather than dynamic recrystallisation.

subfigures.description: EBSD Phase Map with a 50 μm scale bar; legend gives Ferrite (green), Martensite (yellow), Austenite (red). A dominant green ferrite matrix contains elongated, co-aligned yellow martensite and red austenite bands and isolated blocky red austenite grains.

TEM bright-field micrograph (1 μm scale bar) showing a large γ (austenite) grain labelled 1 with an internal dark banded region labelled ά, set in an α (ferrite) matrix; white arrows point to a boundary the caption identifies as an initial ferrite–ferrite boundary. Three SAED insets labelled 1, 2, 2 are appended below with zone axes Z=[001], Z=[011], Z=[111] and indexed reflections [(200), (111), (000)] / [(200), (211), (011), (000)] / [(011), (000), (101), (110)].

Compressive true stress–strain curves with True Stress (MPa) 0–600 versus True Strain 0.0–0.6. Black curve labelled 500 °C peaks between the 500 and 600 MPa gridlines then declines; red curve labelled 600 °C rises to ~400 MPa and stays nearly flat.

Inset line plot of Stress (Mpa) versus Deformation Temperature (°C), x-axis 0–800 with data from 100 to 700 °C, y-axis 0–800. Legend: Maximum Flow Stress (black squares) and Yield Stress (0.2%) (red). Both decrease with temperature and fall steeply between 500 and 600 °C; a blue dashed oval encircles this drop.
